objects.name: Thread
objects.description: A thread of execution is the smallest sequence of programmed instructions that can be managed independently by a scheduler, which is typically part of the operating system. A thread is typically a component of a process. Multiple threads can exist within the same process and share resources such as memory, while different processes do not share these resources. The threads of a process share executable code instructions and context, such as the values of variables at any given moment.

events.definition: The event corresponding to the act of creating a new thread.

fields.name: subject

fields.description: Originating IP address.

fields.name: src_port

fields.name: message_type

fields.name: to

fields.description: the content of the To field in the email header; does not necessarily match up with real recipients.

objects.name: HTTP
objects.description: HTTP events represents requests made over the network via the HTTP protocol.

events.definition: The event corresponding to an HTTP GET request.
The event corresponding to an HTTP POST request.
The event corresponding to an HTTP PUT request.
The event corresponding to an HTTP TUNNEL request.

fields.name: hostname
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: hostname on which the request was seen.

fields.name: request_body_bytes
fields.basis: a decimal integer — CAR: 'represented in decimal notation' (ids, ports, counts, byte sizes, status codes)
fields.description: Integer value corresponding to the total number of bytes in the request.

fields.name: http_version
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: HTTP version that is specified in the header.

fields.name: request_body_content
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: Body of the HTTP request; usually specifies the exact content being requested.

fields.name: request_referrer
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: The URL from which the request was referred, if applicable.

fields.name: requester_ip_address
fields.basis: an IP address as text: IPv4 dotted-quad or RFC 5952 IPv6 (brief §6: no native IP type)
fields.description: IP address from which the request was made.

fields.name: response_body_bytes
fields.basis: a decimal integer — CAR: 'represented in decimal notation' (ids, ports, counts, byte sizes, status codes)
fields.description: Integer value corresponding to the total number of bytes in the response.

fields.name: response_body_content
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: Content of the response (does not include header).

fields.name: response_status_code
fields.basis: a decimal integer — CAR: 'represented in decimal notation' (ids, ports, counts, byte sizes, status codes)
fields.description: HTTP protocol status code in response header

fields.name: url_full
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: URL to which the HTTP request was sent

fields.name: url_domain
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: Domain portion of the URL.

fields.name: url_remainder
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: the path after the root domain

fields.name: url_scheme
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: type of user that initiated the request.

fields.name: user_agent_full
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: User agent string associated with the request

fields.name: user_agent_name
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: The user agent through which the request was made.
fields.example: Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 7.0; SM-G930VC Build/NRD90M; wv) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/4.0 Chrome/58.0.3029.83 Mobile Safari/537.36

fields.name: user_agent_device

fields.name: user_agent_version
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: User Agent Version. Note that some User Agent strings may not label versions in the same way.

objects.name: Socket
objects.description: Socket events are low-level events that may or may not result in a flow. Socket listenining events in particular can be helpful in detecting malicious activity.

events.definition: The event corresponding to a socket binding to a specific address
The event corresponding to a socket being closed.
The event corresponding to a socket being opened into a listening status, usually on a specific local port.

fields.name: pid
fields.basis: a decimal integer — CAR: 'represented in decimal notation' (ids, ports, counts, byte sizes, status codes)
fields.description: ID of the process that acted on the socket

fields.name: image_path
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: Path to the executable that initiated the socket event.

fields.name: success
fields.basis: 'true' or 'false' (CAR examples); empty when not observed — the model's own tri-state
fields.description: Boolean indicator of whether the socket event was successful (e.g. the socket was created as requested)

fields.name: family
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: The type of socket in question

fields.name: protocol
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: The type of connection that was attempted on the socket

fields.name: local_address
fields.basis: an IP address as text: IPv4 dotted-quad or RFC 5952 IPv6 (brief §6: no native IP type)
fields.description: IP address on which the socket will accept connections; does not include the port number.

fields.name: local_port
fields.basis: a decimal integer — CAR: 'represented in decimal notation' (ids, ports, counts, byte sizes, status codes)
fields.description: Port number on which the socket is bound at the local end. This pertains to TCP and UDP sockets but not IP sockets.

fields.name: remote_port
fields.basis: a decimal integer — CAR: 'represented in decimal notation' (ids, ports, counts, byte sizes, status codes)
fields.description: Port number on which the socket is bound at the remote end.

fields.name: remote_address
fields.basis: an IP address as text: IPv4 dotted-quad or RFC 5952 IPv6 (brief §6: no native IP type)
fields.description: IP address with which the socket is communicating on the remote end.

fields.name: local_path
fields.basis: as observed — names, paths, '<DOMAIN>\<USER>', free text; the writer truncates long text so a record stays well under the ~30 KB render limit
fields.description: In the case that a socket is used for local interprocess communication, the socket binds to a local filepath, and will usually be visible in the filesystem. This is the case with AF_UNIX type sockets.

events.definition: The vent corresponding to a process accessing the memory space of another process.

The event corresponding to a process creation in Windows. In the kernel, these are often captured with the callback [PsSetCreateProcessNotifyRoutine](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/hardware/ff559951%28v=vs.85%29.aspx).

The event corresponding to a process destruction in Windows. In the kernel, these are also captured with the callback [PsSetCreateProcessNotifyRoutine](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/hardware/ff559951%28v=vs.85%29.aspx), but with a pointer to a NULL structure.

events.definition: ATT&CK data component “process modification”: A process was modified.
The event corresponding with changing permissions on a file.
The event corresponding to the creation of a file.
The event corresponding to the deletion of a file.
The event corresponding to the modification of a file or its metadata.
The event corresponding to the accessing of a file to be read.
The modification of an attribute, such as creation time. The file metadata may change, but the contents of the file remain the same.
The event corresponding to the accessing of a file in order to write new instructions or information into a file.

events.definition: The event corresponding to the ending of collection of flow data in a given time period.

A flow message pertains to any event between start and end when content is sent over the connection (may imply TCP). This often implies use of traffic content collected via PCAP or a similar mechanism.
The event corresponding to the beginning of collection of flow data in a given time period.
